reader.requirement: When an input-output statement on a sequential file is unsuccessful because of a condition the implementor specifies (none of the successful, at end, permanent error or logic error conditions), the I-O status must report it in the implementor-defined class (9x, VII.1.3.5 GRL2.5); where more than one value applies the implementor picks.

a host refusal of the OPEN answers '61' when the sharing facility is in effect and the 1985 value '30' at 85
the clause-less connector's sharing mode: no restriction at 85 (FileSharing.AllOther)
the file-sharing-facility row (introduced 2002) the three sites above read
ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL refused below 2023 (COBOL0900), so the line-sequential '71' cannot arise at 85
ASSIGN USING refused below 2002 (COBOL0900), so the '31' association failure cannot arise at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 2002 and later a second connector's conflicting OPEN answers '61' (and a host refusal '61'); at 85 the file sharing facility is off, so those OPENs answer '00' or the 1985 '30', and no status outside the 1985 list or 9x is produced for a sequential file

reader.notes: The compiler defines two implementor conditions for sequential files, the LINAGE value violation ('90') and a record character with no byte image in the file's coded character set ('91', with or without CODE-SET), documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-110.md; both make the statement unsuccessful and run the USE declarative. At 85 the 2002 file sharing facility is switched off by DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility, and LINE SEQUENTIAL and ASSIGN USING are refused, so no 2002+ status (61, 51, 71, 31) reaches a 1985 program.
reader.at-2023: ios7 at 2023: 91 the same; ios2 at 2023: the second OPEN of one file answers 61 (the 2002 facility)

refuter.evidence: io6.cob (FD F1 LINAGE IS W-N LINES, W-N = 0; F2 an absent non-optional file) at --std 85 printed: LINAGE-0 OPEN OUTPUT FS=90; SECOND OPEN OUTPUT FS=41; WRITE FS=90; CLOSE FS=00; SECOND CLOSE FS=42; ABSENT OPEN INPUT FS=35; ABSENT SECOND OPEN FS=35; ABSENT CLOSE FS=42. --std 2023 prints the same lines. So the OPEN that reports the implementor-defined 90 has in fact put the file in an open mode (a second OPEN answers 41, the CLOSE answers 00), unlike the genuinely unsuccessful 35 OPEN (second OPEN 35, CLOSE 42). Code: SequentialConnector.BeginLinagePage's summary says 'A violation here does NOT un-open the connector', justified only by §2023:13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 2 ('until the file is closed'); the 1985 LINAGE clause (§1985:VII.3.7.4 GR2/GR3) states the value rules with no such continuation, and nothing on the path consults the edition. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GR5 ["unsuccessfully executed as a result of a condition that is specified by the implementor"]; OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR1 ["The successful execution of an OPEN statement determines the availability of the file and results in the file being in an open mode"]; OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR3 ["When a file is not in an open mode, no statement may be executed which references the file"]; OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.4 ["An OPEN statement is attempted for a file in the open mode"] and ["A CLOSE statement is attempted for a file not in the open mode"]. Other probes found no fault: io1 (OPEN OUTPUT/INPUT/EXTEND in a missing directory 30/35/35), io2 (a directory: 35/37/35), io3 (an unusable file name 30/30), io5 (ADVANCING 0 and PAGE 00): all 1985 values, no 31/61/9x. kb/Work: PB526 (landed) chose the 2023 continuation for every edition and pins it at 85 with conformance-suite/cases/13.18.34-LINAGE/pb526_linage_ec_condition_85 (B-OPEN FS=90 then B-CLOSE FS=00); no note records the 1985 conflict.

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (misleads-diagnosis / wrong-answer; cause a: this edition needs its own arm and has none). At 1985 GR5 defines the 9x class as a statement 'unsuccessfully executed', and only a successful OPEN results in an open mode (§1985:VII.4.3.4 GR1, Table 1). The compiler's 90 OPEN establishes an open mode anyway, so a 1985 program that tests FS = '90' and re-OPENs gets 41, and its CLOSE answers 00 where 42 is the 1985 value. Repro: io6.cob above; expected at 85: second OPEN 90 again (or the OPEN of a file not in open mode), WRITE 48, CLOSE 42; observed 41, 90, 00.

adjudication.reason: An OPEN refused with status 90 (LINAGE of zero) leaves the file open: a second OPEN gives 41, a WRITE 90, the CLOSE 00. At 1985 a 9x statement is unsuccessful, so the WRITE is 48 and the CLOSE 42. The 2023 continuation (kb/Work PB526) is applied at every edition. Checker's confidence: medium-high.
